newsitem.title: USA: Dow to buy Lilly stake in Dow Elanco for $900 million.
newsitem.headline: Dow to buy Lilly stake in Dow Elanco for $900 million.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. said Thursday it will acquire Eli Lilly and Co.'s 40 percent stake in their agricultural chemicals joint venture, Dow Elanco, for $900 million plus $300 million in undistributed earnings.

The $1.2 billion transaction, a result of Lilly's decision to exercise its option to sell its interest, will make Dow the sole owner of the Indianapolis-based operation, which was formed in 1989 and has annual sales of about $2 billion.
The Lilly-Dow deal came a day after Merck & Co. Inc. agreed to sell its agricultural chemicals unit to Switzerland's Novartis AG for $910 million.
Wall Street analysts called the close timing of the deals a coincidence, but added that more mergers and acquisitions can be expected in the world agricultural chemicals industry.
"It is a rapidly consolidating business," said Prudential Securities chemicals analyst Glenn Mierendorf in New York.

Formed in 1989, the Dow Elanco venture combined the plant science businesses of Indianapolis-based Lilly and Midland, Mich.-based Dow, as well as Dow's speciality pest management business. Dow owned 60 percent, and Lilly 40 percent, of the venture, which has seen strong growth in sales and profits.

"We view the agricultural products business as an engine for growth, which will be accelerated by Dow Elanco's increased commitment to agricultural biotechnology," William Stavropoulos, Dow's chief executive officer, said in a statement.
"This acquisition is part of our value growth strategy to increase investment in performance businesses."

Dow, the world's fifth-largest chemical company, called Dow Elanco "one of the world's largest research-based agricultural companies." The company develops, manufactures and markets products for management of weeds, insects and plant disease and for urban pest control.
Dow Elanco also is majority owner of Mycogen Corp., an agricultural biotechnology company that develops and markets technology-based seed and pest management products.
Dow also announced that it would repurchase an additional 20 million shares.

Dow Chemical said the new stock buy-back will begin once the current repurchase authorisation is completed in the second quarter. The shares will be bought on the open market or in private transactions.
Since January 1995, Dow has repurchased 55.3 million shares, equivalent to about 20 percent of its outstanding stock. As of April 30, Dow had 231.9 million shares outstanding.
Dow Chemical's stock fell $1.25 to $87.50 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, while Lilly added 37.5 cents to $93, also on the NYSE.
